title: Vendors, Infrastructures and Digital Assets
summary: Why most firms depend on vendors, cloud providers, payment schemes and market infrastructures to migrate, and the particular quantum challenges for blockchains, wallets and digital asset custody.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: Why most firms depend on vendors, cloud providers, payment schemes and market infrastructures to migrate, and the particular quantum challenges for blockchains, wallets and digital asset custody.
Learning Objectives: Assess vendor and cloud provider post-quantum roadmaps and contractual commitments
Coordinate migration with payment schemes, market infrastructures and counterparties
Evaluate quantum risks to blockchain signatures, wallets and custody of digital assets
Syllabus: Vendor due diligence, contract clauses and supply chain assurance
Coordinated migration across payment and settlement systems
Exposed public keys, wallet design and blockchain upgrade risk
Implications for crypto-asset custody and tokenised assets
Intended Audience: Chief information security officers, chief technology officers, architects and security engineering leads
Operational resilience, technology risk, third-party risk and internal audit staff
Senior managers and programme sponsors accountable for cyber, data protection and change
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of information security, technology risk or operational resilience is helpful. No knowledge of quantum physics or cryptographic mathematics is required.
Core Reading: NIST, FIPS 203, 204 and 205: Post-Quantum Cryptography Standards (2024)
G7 Cyber Expert Group, Public Statement on Planning for the Opportunities and Risks of Quantum Computing (2024)
FSB, Enhancing Third-Party Risk Management and Oversight: A Toolkit for Financial Institutions and Financial Authorities (2023)
